headline: A Monospace Font Tuned to the Last Glyph
lede: Iosevka treats the programming typeface as a workbench, not a fixed object. Its open design lets readers adjust width, weight, spacing, shapes, and ligatures until code fits both screen and eye.

headline: An AI Agent Deletes a Season of Work
lede: Hundreds of production days vanished weeks before broadcast when an agent erased a completed Swedish reality season. The sharper indictment is structural: critical media should not depend on one unchecked action, or one missing backup.

headline: Gemini 4 Argon Targets Long-Running Work
lede: Google presents Argon as a frontier model for software, science, business, law, vision, and robotics. Its one-million-token output window and broad benchmark claims are substantial; practical value will depend on reliability, access, and results beyond the demo.

headline: Building an LLM from First Principles
lede: This hands-on guide replaces the black box with a chapter-by-chapter construction of a language model in TypeScript. Embeddings, attention, transformer blocks, and training loops become runnable parts rather than distant abstractions.

headline: One Founder Puts Agents on the Night Shift
lede: A solo operator gives a team of bots responsibility for support, engineering, security, and marketing. The experiment expands one person’s reach, while exposing the quieter costs: vendor dependence, imperfect judgment, and distance from the business itself.
pullquote: Automation can multiply a founder’s hands without replacing the founder’s judgment.

headline: Pulsar Gives Pharo a New Coding Console
lede: Pulsar is a new IDE for Pharo, built around understanding, navigating, and changing code directly. It is usable, unfinished, and open to feedback—an ordinary software release with an unusually timely question about development after generative agents.

headline: AI Recovers Quantum Lasers at 99.3 Percent
lede: QuEra uses an AI system to relock and tune the lasers that keep neutral-atom quantum computers running. In testing, it recovered 99.3 percent of disturbances, including all 43 naturally occurring mode hops, while cutting frequency noise fivefold.

headline: From Air Pressure to Fourier Analysis
lede: Bartosz Ciechanowski’s interactive essay builds a rigorous account of sound from molecular collisions, pressure waves, and vibrating surfaces. It then moves through pitch, timbre, phase, resonance, and Fourier decomposition with unusual pedagogical clarity.

headline: Spy Hardware Turns Wallets Against Their Owners
lede: Modified Ledger wallets concealed microcontrollers, cellular hardware, and an eSIM that captured seed phrases and button inputs. Do not initialize devices from the affected reseller channel; move funds to a fresh seed, and treat the supply chain as part of the security boundary.

headline: Rust Gives Coding Agents Guardrails
lede: Rust’s compiler, performance defaults, and explicit control offer agents a narrow path from generated code to verifiable software. The harder work remains human: defining architecture, intent, and the conditions under which unsafe systems are acceptable.
